title.en: Used to: when I was a child

ex.t: Früher spielte ich jeden Tag Fußball.
ex.ko: 나는 어릴 때 매일 축구를 하곤 했어요.
ex.en: I used to play football every day when I was a child.

ex.t: Wir wohnten in einem kleinen Dorf.
ex.en: We lived in a small village.

ex.t: Ich fuhr mit dem Fahrrad zur Schule.
ex.ko: 나는 자전거를 타고 학교에 가곤 했어요.
ex.en: I used to go to school by bike.
I had a lot of toys.

ex.ko: 나는 매일 아침 만화를 보곤 했어요.
ex.en: I used to watch cartoons every morning.

ex.ko: 나는 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
ex.en: I don't live there any more.
In the past people wrote letters.

explain.ko: 지금은 사라진 과거의 습관과 상태는 früher / damals + Präteritum으로 말합니다. 지금과의 차이는 nicht mehr (더 이상 ~ 않다)로 나타냅니다: Ich wohne nicht mehr dort. 일상 대화에서는 Perfekt를 쓰지만, sein·haben과 이야기체에서는 Präteritum이 자연스럽습니다.
explain.en: Talk about habits and states that are no longer true with früher / damals + Präteritum. Show the change with nicht mehr: Ich wohne nicht mehr dort. In everyday speech Perfekt is common, but with sein and haben and in stories the Präteritum is natural.

rows: Früher spielte ich jeden Tag Fußball.

notes.ko: früher는 문장 앞이나 동사 뒤에 둡니다.
notes.en: Früher goes at the start or after the verb.
Früher and damals mark the past.

lines.t: Wo wohntest du, als du ein Kind warst?

trans.en: (Question) Where did you live when you were a child?

options: Ich wohnte in einem kleinen Dorf.

lines.t: Was machtest du früher als Kind?

trans.en: (Question) What did you use to do when you were a child?

lines.t: Welche Zeichentrickfilme hast du als Kind gesehen?
Ich sah Tierfilme. Jetzt sehe ich sie nicht mehr.
Ich auch nicht mehr. Und ich fuhr mit dem Fahrrad zur Schule.
Ich ging zu Fuß zur Schule.

trans.ko:
A: 어릴 때 어떤 만화를 보곤 했어?
B: 나는 동물 만화를 보곤 했어. 지금은 안 봐.
A: 나도 그랬어. 그리고 자전거를 타고 학교에 갔어.
B: 나는 걸어서 학교에 가곤 했어.
trans.en:
A: What cartoons did you use to watch when you were a child?
B: I used to watch animal cartoons. I don't watch them now.
A: Me too. And I used to go to school by bike.
B: I used to walk to school.

lines.t: Als ich ein Kind war, wohnte ich in einem kleinen Dorf. Die Nachbarn waren alle nett. Ich spielte jeden Tag draußen mit meinen Freunden. Jetzt wohne ich in einer Stadt, also wohne ich nicht mehr dort.

trans.ko: 나는 어릴 때 작은 마을에 살곤 했어요. 이웃들은 모두 친절했어요. 나는 매일 친구들과 밖에서 놀곤 했어요. 지금은 도시에 살아서 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
trans.en: When I was a child, I used to live in a small village. The neighbours were all kind. I used to play outside with my friends every day. Now I live in a city, so I don't live there any more.

lines.t: Wohnten Sie früher in dieser Stadt?

trans.ko:
직원: 예전에 이 도시에 살았어요?
손님: 네, 열 살까지 살았어요.
직원: 학교는 어떻게 다녔어요?
손님: 자전거를 타고 다녔어요.
trans.en:
Clerk: Did you use to live in this city?
Guest: Yes, until I was ten.
Clerk: How did you get to school?
Guest: I used to go by bike.

items.passage:
1) Früher ___ ich jeden Tag Fußball.
2) Wir ___ in einem kleinen Dorf.
3) Ich wohne ___ dort.

trans.ko: 1) 나는 어릴 때 매일 축구를 하곤 했어요. 2) 우리는 작은 마을에 살았어요. 3) 나는 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
trans.en: 1) I used to play football every day when I was a child. 2) We used to live in a small village. 3) I don't live there any more.

items.passage: Als ich ein Kind war, (1) ich in einem kleinen Dorf. Ich spielte jeden Tag (2) mit meinen Freunden. Jetzt wohne ich in einer Stadt, also wohne ich (3) dort.

trans.ko: 나는 어릴 때 작은 마을에 살곤 했어요. 나는 매일 친구들과 밖에서 놀곤 했어요. 지금은 도시에 살아서 더 이상 거기 안 살아요.
trans.en: When I was a child, I used to live in a small village. I used to play outside with my friends every day. Now I live in a city, so I don't live there any more.

items.passage:
NOTIZ AN EINEN FREUND
Als Kind fuhr ich mit dem Fahrrad zur Schule.
Jetzt nehme ich den Bus.

trans.ko:
친구에게 쓴 메모
어릴 때 나는 자전거를 타고 학교에 가곤 했어. 지금은 버스를 타.
trans.en:
NOTE TO A FRIEND
When I was a child, I used to go to school by bike. Now I take the bus.

items.passage: Als Tom ein Kind war, wohnte er in einem kleinen Dorf. Er spielte jeden Tag Fußball. Jetzt wohnt er in einer großen Stadt.

trans.ko: 톰은 어릴 때 작은 마을에 살았어요. 그는 매일 축구를 하곤 했어요. 지금 그는 큰 도시에 살아요.
trans.en: When Tom was a child, he lived in a small village. He used to play football every day. Now he lives in a big city.
